text.headline: Copper prices tumble amid trade tensions
text.tone: Sharp moves in industrial commodities reflect growing sensitivity to global trade rhetoric, even as broader equity and bond markets remain largely range-bound.
lead: Copper fell 3.6% to $12,750/t on Wednesday, the most significant move on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]]. This decline coincided with a 11.1% rise in the VIX volatility index in the latest data. While copper slumped, silver and platinum posted modest gains of less than 1%.

The weakness in copper is consistent with confirmed concerns regarding US–China trade and tariffs. Recent headlines highlighted legislative efforts to end China's trade status and disputes over green energy products. Such developments typically weigh on global growth expectations and industrial demand.

Broader markets showed less conviction. US large caps fell 0.2%, and the US 10-year yield declined by 2 bp in the latest data. The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] notes that while world stocks remain below their 200-day average, this session lacked the uniform selling seen in previous downturns.

Future sessions will clarify if the copper sell-off signals deeper industrial cooling. Continued pressure on the yuan or further spikes in volatility would support the trade-tension interpretation. The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] places these moves within the context of the current risk-off regime.

briefs.markets: The VIX volatility index climbed 11.1% in the latest data, while US large caps slipped 0.2% on the [[markets|Financial Markets]] page.
briefs.energy: Natural gas fell 3.1% to $3.10 in the latest data, while crude prices remained nearly flat on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]].
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin fell 1.5% to $63,898 as November ETF outflows reached $2.9B, according to the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] monitor.
briefs.metals: Copper dropped 3.6% to $12,750/t, diverging from modest gains in silver and platinum on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]].
briefs.estate: The [[estate|Estate Index]] shows China house prices falling 6.3% annually, contrasting with a 33.7% surge in Moldova.
briefs.corporate: APA Corporation earned a top EB Score of 89 as credit spreads remained calm on the [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]].
briefs.outlook: The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] identifies semiconductors as the weakest theme this quarter, down 24.8% amid a broader risk-off regime.
briefs.islamic: The EB Shariah US 100 outperformed the broader market on a YTD basis, despite a 0.01% dip on the [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] page.
